blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the advanced level, Incoterms stop being a paperwork exercise and become a language — a surprisingly precise one — for allocating risk between two sophisticated counterparties. Each Incoterm is, in effect, a compact contract: who pays, who insures, who bears loss, and, crucially, at which geographic point the balance tips.

Rarely do experienced negotiators fight about the choice of Incoterm per se. What they debate is the line of risk transfer, and whether the selected term really matches the economic realities of the route: a long voyage through contested waters, a supplier nervous about local unrest, a buyer with superior insurance relationships, a route with notorious port delays.

Sometimes the answer is to take the standard Incoterm but to modify it, carefully, in the contract. Sometimes it is to use a non-standard term and to document the allocation explicitly. Either way, the instinct is the same: never let three letters do the work of a real conversation, and never let the convenience of a label hide a mis-priced risk on either side.

items.q: According to the text, at the advanced level an Incoterm functions primarily as…
options: a language for allocating risk between counterparties
a customs formality with no commercial weight
a fixed price agreed by both sides
items.why: "become a language… for allocating risk between two sophisticated counterparties."

items.q: What do experienced negotiators actually debate, according to the text?
options: The line of risk transfer and whether the term fits the route
items.why: "What they debate is the line of risk transfer, and whether the selected term really matches the economic realities of the route."

items.q: The text presents two possible responses when a standard term does not fit. They are…
options: change the supplier, or change the buyer
modify the standard term in the contract, or use a non-standard term documented explicitly
abandon the deal, or accept the risk silently
insure twice, or cancel the voyage
items.why: "take the standard Incoterm but modify it… or use a non-standard term and document the allocation explicitly."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Standard terms sometimes require careful modification.
A convenient term may conceal a mis-priced risk.
A familiar three-letter label can safely replace a detailed negotiation.
The geographic point of risk transfer deserves close scrutiny.
items.why: Inferência: o texto encerra advertindo para nunca deixar três letras fazerem o trabalho de uma conversa real.

items.q: The examples of "contested waters" and "notorious port delays" are given to suggest that…
options: insurance is always the buyer's responsibility
long voyages are best avoided entirely
the right term depends on the concrete economics of the route, not the label
items.why: Inferência: os exemplos mostram por que a escolha precisa refletir a realidade econômica da rota, não uma sigla padrão.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry conduzindo a revisão dos Incoterms para a nova rota Ásia–Europa. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, thank you all for making the time. Before legal walks us through the draft, let me frame what we are actually deciding today, because it is not, in my view, which three letters we type into the contract.

This new Asia-Europe lane runs through waters that have been anything but quiet this year. So the real question is where, precisely, the risk should pass from us to the buyer — and whether the term we have pencilled in reflects that. On paper, CIF looks tidy. In practice, our insurance relationships are far stronger than theirs, which tells me we may be handing them a cost they would pay dearly to carry.

Here is what I would like from this room. Operations: give me the honest delay profile at the discharge ports, not the brochure version. Legal: draft the modification language so that, if we keep the standard term, the transfer point is spelled out and not merely implied. And let us pressure-test one non-standard allocation as an alternative, so we are choosing, not defaulting.

Never again do I want a label to quietly mis-price a risk on either side. Let us make the conversation do the work, and let the letters simply record it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Harry frame the real decision facing the room?
options: Which three letters to type into the contract
Whether to use the Asia-Europe lane at all
Where the risk should pass and whether the term reflects that
Which insurer offers the lowest premium
items.why: "the real question is where, precisely, the risk should pass… and whether the term we have pencilled in reflects that."

items.q: Why is Harry sceptical of CIF for this deal, despite it looking "tidy"?
options: Because their own insurance relationships are far stronger than the buyer's
Because the buyer refused CIF outright
Because CIF is more expensive to document
Because CIF is banned on this route
items.why: "our insurance relationships are far stronger than theirs… we may be handing them a cost they would pay dearly to carry."

items.q: What does Harry ask the operations team for specifically?
options: The honest delay profile at the discharge ports
items.why: "give me the honest delay profile at the discharge ports, not the brochure version."

items.q: When Harry says he wants the team "choosing, not defaulting," he implies that…
options: the team should always pick the cheapest option
deciding by habit risks accepting an ill-fitting term without thought
the standard term is always correct
items.why: Inferência: testar uma alternativa não-padrão força uma escolha consciente, em vez de aceitar a sigla por inércia.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's overall stance?
options: Indifferent to the choice of term
Determined to abandon standard Incoterms entirely
Rigorous — he wants the term to record a real negotiation, not replace it
Focused only on cutting insurance costs
items.why: Inferência: ele quer a conversa fazendo o trabalho e as letras apenas registrando — rigor, não rejeição das siglas.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The whole negotiation was really an exercise in risk allocation." Risk allocation is…
options: deciding which side bears which risks
items.why: Risk allocation = alocação de risco: definir qual parte assume cada risco.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Both are sophisticated ___, so neither expects to be protected from its own commercial judgement."
items.why: Counterparty = contraparte, cada lado do contrato.

items.q: "The dispute turned on the exact transfer point." The transfer point is…
options: the moment the invoice is paid
the geographic point at which risk passes from one side to the other
the port where the ship is refuelled
items.why: Transfer point = ponto de transferência: onde o risco passa de uma parte à outra.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A convenient label can quietly hide a ___ risk that one side will regret carrying."
items.why: Mis-priced = mal precificado: um risco cujo custo não foi corretamente avaliado.

items.q: "We took the standard term but chose to modify it in the contract." To modify means to…
items.why: To modify = modificar: alterar o termo de forma deliberada e cuidadosa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações de comércio internacional. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the modified allocation." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two of the regional heads pushed back on the choice of Incoterm." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We will roll out the new allocation model on the next three lanes first." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, lançar por etapas.

items.q: "The team agreed the modification but never followed through on the contract wording." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Renaming the term without changing the transfer point will not move the needle on our exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
